question: Should OpenClaw adopt opt-in Discord source-message subagent progress as a core-supported feature, including the new channel lifecycle, delivery-context, persisted-state, and configuration contracts?
rationale: Patch quality cannot decide whether this user-visible behavior and its permanent plugin/config API surface belong in core; the Discord and subagent owners must choose the long-term contract before merge.

options.title: Sponsor the proposed contract
options.body: Approve the opt-in feature and its generic lifecycle seam, then require an exact-main refresh and green compatibility/delivery validation before landing.

options.title: Narrow the public surface
options.body: Keep the Discord feature but rework it to minimize or internalize the generic plugin and persisted-state contracts before review resumes.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Close the PR if maintainers do not want source-message subagent progress or the associated configuration burden in core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the proposed contract
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in feature and its generic lifecycle seam, then require an exact-main refresh and green compatibility/delivery validation before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The user-facing semantics and configuration are Discord-specific, while the agents/subagents owner can co-review the shared lifecycle portion.
